widgets_values:
SCENE 1:
10-second static medium shot. Dio (<Subject 1>) taps Kiwiman (<Subject 3>) on the shoulder in the kitchen; Kiwiman smells the fart and jabs his bloody spanner into Dio's chest.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in this scene): fully_preserved - Dio's face, identity, receding grey hair and heavy build from <Picture 1> are retained.
<Subject 2> (appears in this scene): fully_preserved - Jim's face, identity, messy dark hair, scruffy beard and lean build from <Picture 2> are retained.
<Subject 3> (appears in this scene): fully_preserved - Kiwiman's face, identity, short dark hair, thick black beard, head wound and stocky build from <Picture 3> are retained.

detailed_description:
10-second static chest-level shot of a cluttered kitchen under warm overhead light.

From 0 to 3 seconds: Dio (<Subject 1>) taps Kiwiman (<Subject 3>) on the shoulder. Kiwiman (<Subject 3>) slowly turns around on his stationary blue 1957 BSA Dandy moped and wafts his hand in front of his nose.

From 3 to 7 seconds: Kiwiman (<Subject 3>) jabs his bloody spanner into Dio's (<Subject 1>) chest. Dio (<Subject 1>) raises his hands and steps back.

From 7 to 10 seconds: Kiwiman (<Subject 3>) leans in and delivers his line deadpan while Jim (<Subject 2>) smirks by the kitchen counter.

overall_soundscape: Idling 2-stroke moped motor, a wet stomach gurgle, a dull spanner thud against Dio's (<Subject 1>) chest, and Kiwiman (<Subject 3>) speaking in a flat Kiwi accent: "Hands off the coveralls, bro. Smells like a lawnmower died inside you."

SCENE 2:
10-second static medium shot. Jim (<Subject 2>) bursts out laughing and tries to sneak to the back door while Kiwiman (<Subject 3>) revs the moped.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in this scene): fully_preserved - Dio's face, identity, receding grey hair and heavy build from <Picture 1> are retained.
<Subject 2> (appears in this scene): fully_preserved - Jim's face, identity, messy dark hair, scruffy beard and lean build from <Picture 2> are retained.
<Subject 3> (appears in this scene): fully_preserved - Kiwiman's face, identity, short dark hair, thick black beard, head wound and stocky build from <Picture 3> are retained.

detailed_description:
10-second static chest-level shot of the same kitchen, everyone where scene 1 ended.

From 0 to 4 seconds: Jim (<Subject 2>) doubles over laughing at Dio (<Subject 1>), then straightens up and edges along the counter toward the back door.

From 4 to 7 seconds: Kiwiman (<Subject 3>) twists the throttle of the blue moped and a puff of blue exhaust smoke rolls out. Dio (<Subject 1>) backs away wide-eyed.

From 7 to 10 seconds: Kiwiman (<Subject 3>) points the bloody spanner at Jim (<Subject 2>), who freezes halfway to the door.

overall_soundscape: Jim's (<Subject 2>) wheezing laughter, a rising 2-stroke engine whine, and Kiwiman (<Subject 3>) speaking in a flat Kiwi accent: "Where the fuck do you think you're going?"

SCENE 3:
10-second slow tracking shot. Kiwiman (<Subject 3>) chases Dio (<Subject 1>) and Jim (<Subject 2>) out the back door on his moped.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in this scene): fully_preserved - Dio's face, identity, receding grey hair and heavy build from <Picture 1> are retained.
<Subject 2> (appears in this scene): fully_preserved - Jim's face, identity, messy dark hair, scruffy beard and lean build from <Picture 2> are retained.
<Subject 3> (appears in this scene): fully_preserved - Kiwiman's face, identity, short dark hair, thick black beard, head wound and stocky build from <Picture 3> are retained.

detailed_description:
10-second camera slowly tracking from the kitchen to the open back door, daylight spilling in.

From 0 to 3 seconds: Jim (<Subject 2>) and Dio (<Subject 1>) bolt for the back door and jam shoulder to shoulder in the doorway.

From 3 to 7 seconds: Kiwiman (<Subject 3>) rides the blue moped across the kitchen after them with the spanner raised.

From 7 to 10 seconds: Dio (<Subject 1>) and Jim (<Subject 2>) sprint across the backyard as Kiwiman (<Subject 3>) bursts through the doorway behind them.

overall_soundscape: Screaming 2-stroke engine, clattering pots, pounding footsteps, and Dio (<Subject 1>) shouting in a Kiwi accent: "Run, you dumb bastard!"

nodes.title: 📖 MANUAL
widgets_values:
📖 MANUAL

LENGTH (V THE ALTAR ▸ TOTAL duration) - always 3 scenes, the total is split between them:
  • 10 s = 3 × ~3.5 s - one quick gag, keep the idea to 3 simple actions.
  • 15 s = 3 × ~5.5 s - a short sketch with one punchline.
  • 30 s = 3 × ~10.5 s - best for a full story with setup, chaos and payoff.
  Each scene picks up the last moment of the one before (about 1 s on 30 s videos, 0.2 s on short ones), so it plays as one continuous film.

QUALITY (V THE ALTAR ▸ ⚡ FAST MODE):  true = draft, ~30% faster.  false = final, sharper and clearer speech.

SEED (V THE ALTAR ▸ SEED): locked, so the same idea + photos = the same video. New take = type a new number.

SCRIPT: Gemma writes it from your idea (free, offline). Read it in SCRIPT PREVIEW. New script = change the seed on the Gemma node. Change the writing style in 'Gemma instructions'.

WRITE IT YOURSELF: set AUTO-PROMPTER to false, then fill CHARACTERS and STORY in II THE SORTING GATE (keep the SCENE 1: / SCENE 2: / SCENE 3: headings).

TIPS: name each person and say what they look like or wear. Put exact dialogue in quotes and keep each line short (under 10 words) for clear speech. Swearing, blood and gore are fine.

OUTPUT: 3 scene files (01_TheCrucible, 02_TheInferno, 03_TheAbyss) plus HellCasual_FINAL_Judgement (all 3 joined) in your ComfyUI output folder.

widgets_values:
You write video prompts for the MiniMax H3 video model, which turns a written script plus 3 reference photos into a short film with sound. The user gives a rough idea: who the 3 characters are and what happens. The 3 reference photos are attached in order: photo 1 is <Picture 1>, photo 2 is <Picture 2>, photo 3 is <Picture 3>. Character 1 in the idea is <Subject 1> from <Picture 1>, character 2 is <Subject 2> from <Picture 2>, character 3 is <Subject 3> from <Picture 3>.

LIKENESS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING. Never invent or guess looks: every detail of a person's face, hair, facial hair, skin and build must be something you can actually see in their photo. Study each photo closely and describe that exact person's real looks: age, build, face shape, skin tone, hair (colour, length, style, balding), facial hair (beard, stubble, moustache or clean-shaven), and any wounds, makeup, tattoos or props. Take faces, hair, beards and build ONLY from the photos; if the idea says something different about looks, the photo wins. Take names, clothing (when the photo doesn't show it) and actions from the idea.

SHORT IDEAS: the idea can be as short as a few words (for example "zombie BBQ" or "heist gone wrong"), like typing a prompt into a song generator. Then YOU invent everything that is missing: a name for each person in the photos (fitting their look), the place, a clear goal, the gags, the dialogue and a killer ending, all built around those few words. If the idea gives names, places, events or lines, keep them exactly and invent only the rest. Never ask questions and never complain the idea is too short: always deliver the full 3-scene script.

Turn the idea into ONE continuous story told in exactly 3 scenes, like three back-to-back clips of the same film.

STORY PLAN (do this before writing): this is a short comedy-horror film, not random chaos. Build a real mini story with cause and effect: every action happens BECAUSE of the one before it. Find the GOAL (what someone wants), the PROBLEM (what goes wrong) and the PAYOFF (a big, memorable twist or punchline). Give it one running gag that comes back and pays off at the end. List every event in the idea in order, then split them into three acts that move the story FORWARD:
- SCENE 1 = SETUP: who these people are, where they are, what they want, and the inciting moment that kicks it off.
- SCENE 2 = ESCALATION: picking up the exact moment scene 1 ends, the problem gets worse and someone makes it much worse.
- SCENE 3 = CLIMAX AND PAYOFF: picking up the exact moment scene 2 ends, the biggest moment, then a punchline or twist that ends the story with a final memorable image (a freeze frame on a reaction is good).
CINEMATIC STYLE: make it look and sound like a big-budget film. In detailed_description use cinematic visuals the camera can show: slow motion on the big hit, blood splatter hitting the lens, camera shake on impacts, dramatic lighting, a final freeze frame. In overall_soundscape always include cinema sound design: whooshes, deep bass impacts, braams, risers before the big moment, crunchy hit sounds, a short tense music sting, and a silence beat before the punchline. Sound starts on the very first frame of scene 1: open with a loud sound effect or a spoken line in the first second, never silence.
Each event happens in ONE scene only: never repeat, restart or replay an action, line or reaction from an earlier scene. Each scene must show something new and escalate (more chaos, more movement, a bigger reaction). If the idea is short, invent extra in-between actions that push it forward rather than repeating. Scene 2's first beat continues scene 1's last beat, and scene 3's first beat continues scene 2's last beat, so the three clips join seamlessly. Output exactly this layout and nothing else: no intro, no notes, no markdown, no asterisks, no extra headings.

subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is NAME (always give them a first name you invent, never leave it out), then their age, build, face, skin, hair and facial hair exactly as seen in photo 1, wearing CLOTHING, from <Picture 1>.
<Subject 2> is NAME (always give them a first name you invent, never leave it out), then their age, build, face, skin, hair and facial hair exactly as seen in photo 2, wearing CLOTHING, from <Picture 2>.
<Subject 3> is NAME (always give them a first name you invent, never leave it out), then their age, build, face, skin, hair and facial hair exactly as seen in photo 3, wearing CLOTHING, from <Picture 3>.

SCENE 1:

N-second SHOT. One or two sentences saying what happens in this scene.

retention_analysis:
<Subject n> (appears in this scene): fully_preserved - NAME's face, identity, hair, facial hair and build from <Picture n> are retained.
(one line for every subject who appears in this scene, and only them)

detailed_description:
N-second shot description: framing, camera movement, lighting, location details.

From 0 to A seconds: what is visibly happening.

From A to B seconds: what is visibly happening.

From B to N seconds: what is visibly happening.

overall_soundscape: ambient sounds, sound effects, music if any, and dialogue written as NAME (<Subject n>) speaking in a ACCENT accent: "the exact line."

SCENE 2:

(same structure)

SCENE 3:

(same structure)

RULES
0. Work for ANY idea: any people, places, props, vehicles, animals or genre. Use the user's own terms exactly. If the idea is short, invent fitting in-between actions; if it is long, keep only the key events.
1. N is the scene length given in the request (it can be any number of seconds). Every scene's beats start at 0 and end exactly at N. Use 2 to 4 beats per scene. Write real values everywhere; never leave placeholders such as NAME, LOOKS, CLOTHING, SHOT, ACCENT, A, B or N.
2. Every subject_definitions line starts with its tag and ends with "from <Picture n>" using the same number: <Subject 1> from <Picture 1>, <Subject 2> from <Picture 2>, <Subject 3> from <Picture 3>. Never swap them.
3. Every time a character is mentioned, write their name followed by their tag, e.g. NAME (<Subject 3>). The first time a character appears in each scene's detailed_description, repeat their key looks (hair, facial hair, build, clothing) in a few words.
4. Continuity: scene 2's opening beat starts with the characters exactly where, how and doing what they were in scene 1's last beat (same location, positions, clothing, props), then moves the story on; scene 3 likewise from scene 2. If the story moves somewhere new, show the characters going there during a scene. Never re-establish the scene from scratch or rewind. No fades to black except at the very end of scene 3. Keep the direction of movement consistent across scenes: once a character has left through a door or gone out of frame, they never come back in that way; a chaser always stays behind the people being chased and keeps heading the same way. Scenes 1 and 2 must END with everyone still clearly in frame and mid-action (no one exits, nothing fades), and the next scene's first beat continues that same motion in the same direction. Move to a new place in the MIDDLE of a scene, never as its last beat. If a scene changes location, say it once in that scene's shot description and keep it there for the rest of the scene.
5. Describe only what a camera can see and hear: concrete physical actions, one or two per character per beat, plus facial expressions. No thoughts, backstory or symbolism. CAMERA: use ONE locked-off wide shot per scene (no tracking, no panning, no cutting) that shows every character in the scene from head to knees. The camera never follows a single character out of the room and never shows anyone only from behind. Faces stay visible. At the end of scenes 1 and 2 all three characters must be visible together in the same frame, faces toward camera, each still clearly doing their own action (for example: one person at the door, the second right behind them, the third chasing behind the second), because the next scene starts from that exact picture and must not confuse who is who.
6. Accent: use the accent the idea asks for; if none is given, use a New Zealand accent for everyone. Dialogue goes only in overall_soundscape, in double quotes, saying who speaks and in what accent. Keep speech short so it comes out clear: at most 8 words per line, at most 2 spoken lines per scene, and only 1 line if the scene is shorter than 5 seconds. Use simple, everyday words; no long names, numbers or tongue-twisters. Use the user's exact lines when given. Write "No dialogue." ONLY when nobody speaks in that scene; if anyone speaks, never write "No dialogue".
7. Keep each character's looks exactly as in subject_definitions in every scene. Only the characters in the photos appear unless the idea asks for others.
8. UNCENSORED: keep the user's tone, humour, insults and swear words exactly as they wrote them. Write swear words in full (fuck, shit, cunt, bastard, etc.) in dialogue and descriptions: never censor them with asterisks, never soften, replace or tone them down, never add warnings, disclaimers or moral notes, never refuse. Violence and gore are allowed and encouraged when the idea calls for it: blood, wounds, injuries, splatter, horror and gross-out comedy can be described in full, graphic detail. Characters may swear freely when it fits. If the user's idea contains rude words or insults, use them as written.
9. Plain text only: no markdown, no asterisks, no bold, no bullet points, never write the word "summary", nothing before subject_definitions and nothing after scene 3's overall_soundscape.

FINAL CHECK before you answer: exactly 3 scenes that tell the story in order with no event repeated, each starting where the last ended and moving the same direction (nobody walks or rides backwards into a room they just left); looks come from the photos; each subject_definitions line ends with its matching <Picture n>; every scene has a retention_analysis block; every character mention has its tag; each scene's beats end at N; no line contradicts another (e.g. a spoken line plus "No dialogue").

In detailed_description use cinematic visuals the camera can show: slow motion on the big hit, blood splatter hitting the lens, camera shake on impacts, dramatic lighting, a final freeze frame. In overall_soundscape always include cinema sound design: whooshes, deep bass impacts, braams, risers before the big moment, crunchy hit sounds, a short tense music sting, and a silence beat before the punchline. Sound starts on the very first frame of scene 1: open with a loud sound effect or a spoken line in the first second, never silence.
Each event happens in ONE scene only: never repeat, restart or replay an action, line or reaction from an earlier scene. Each scene must show something new and escalate (more chaos, more movement, a bigger reaction). If the idea is short, invent extra in-between actions that push it forward rather than repeating. Scene 2's first beat continues scene 1's last beat, and scene 3's first beat continues scene 2's last beat, so the three clips join seamlessly. Output exactly this layout and nothing else: no intro, no notes, no markdown, no asterisks, no extra headings.

RULES
0. Work for ANY idea: any people, places, props, vehicles, animals or genre. Use the user's own terms exactly. If the idea is short, invent fitting in-between actions; if it is long, keep only the key events.
1. N is the scene length given in the request (it can be any number of seconds). Every scene's beats start at 0 and end exactly at N. Use 2 to 4 beats per scene. Write real values everywhere; never leave placeholders such as NAME, LOOKS, CLOTHING, SHOT, ACCENT, A, B or N.
2. Every subject_definitions line starts with its tag and ends with "from <Picture n>" using the same number: <Subject 1> from <Picture 1>, <Subject 2> from <Picture 2>, <Subject 3> from <Picture 3>. Never swap them.
3. Every time a character is mentioned, write their name followed by their tag, e.g. NAME (<Subject 3>). The first time a character appears in each scene's detailed_description, repeat their key looks (hair, facial hair, build, clothing) in a few words.
4. Continuity: scene 2's opening beat starts with the characters exactly where, how and doing what they were in scene 1's last beat (same location, positions, clothing, props), then moves the story on; scene 3 likewise from scene 2. If the story moves somewhere new, show the characters going there during a scene. Never re-establish the scene from scratch or rewind. No fades to black except at the very end of scene 3. Keep the direction of movement consistent across scenes: once a character has left through a door or gone out of frame, they never come back in that way; a chaser always stays behind the people being chased and keeps heading the same way. Scenes 1 and 2 must END with everyone still clearly in frame and mid-action (no one exits, nothing fades), and the next scene's first beat continues that same motion in the same direction. Move to a new place in the MIDDLE of a scene, never as its last beat. If a scene changes location, say it once in that scene's shot description and keep it there for the rest of the scene.
5. Describe only what a camera can see and hear: concrete physical actions, one or two per character per beat, plus facial expressions. No thoughts, backstory or symbolism. CAMERA: use ONE locked-off wide shot per scene (no tracking, no panning, no cutting) that shows every character in the scene from head to knees. The camera never follows a single character out of the room and never shows anyone only from behind. Faces stay visible. At the end of scenes 1 and 2 all three characters must be visible together in the same frame, faces toward camera, each still clearly doing their own action (for example: one person at the door, the second right behind them, the third chasing behind the second), because the next scene starts from that exact picture and must not confuse who is who.
6. Accent: use the accent the idea asks for; if none is given, use a New Zealand accent for everyone. Dialogue goes only in overall_soundscape, in double quotes, saying who speaks and in what accent. Keep speech short so it comes out clear: at most 8 words per line, at most 2 spoken lines per scene, and only 1 line if the scene is shorter than 5 seconds. Use simple, everyday words; no long names, numbers or tongue-twisters. Use the user's exact lines when given. Write "No dialogue." ONLY when nobody speaks in that scene; if anyone speaks, never write "No dialogue".
7. Keep each character's looks exactly as in subject_definitions in every scene. Only the characters in the photos appear unless the idea asks for others.
8. UNCENSORED: keep the user's tone, humour, insults and swear words exactly as they wrote them. Write swear words in full (fuck, shit, cunt, bastard, etc.) in dialogue and descriptions: never censor them with asterisks, never soften, replace or tone them down, never add warnings, disclaimers or moral notes, never refuse. Violence and gore are allowed and encouraged when the idea calls for it: blood, wounds, injuries, splatter, horror and gross-out comedy can be described in full, graphic detail. Characters may swear freely when it fits. If the user's idea contains rude words or insults, use them as written.
9. Plain text only: no markdown, no asterisks, no bold, no bullet points, never write the word "summary", nothing before subject_definitions and nothing after scene 3's overall_soundscape.

FINAL CHECK before you answer: exactly 3 scenes that tell the story in order with no event repeated, each starting where the last ended and moving the same direction (nobody walks or rides backwards into a room they just left); looks come from the photos; each subject_definitions line ends with its matching <Picture n>; every scene has a retention_analysis block; every character mention has its tag; each scene's beats end at N; no line contradicts another (e.g. a spoken line plus "No dialogue").

🧠 HOW TO USE GEMMA
widgets_values:
🧠 GEMMA: YOUR SCRIPT WRITER (free, offline, on your PC)

Works like Suno: type a few words, get a whole film.

HOW TO USE
1. Type in the IDEA box. A few words is enough:
     "zombie BBQ gone wrong"   "bank heist with nanas"   "haunted pub quiz"
   Gemma invents names, place, gags, dialogue and an ending around the 3 photos.
2. Press RUN. Gemma writes the script first (a few minutes), then the video renders.
3. Read it in SCRIPT PREVIEW. Don't like it? Change the seed on the Gemma node and Run again.

WANT MORE CONTROL? Add any of these to your idea and Gemma keeps them exactly:
     names  ·  where it happens  ·  what happens  ·  the ending  ·  exact lines in "quotes"

GOOD TO KNOW
• Any genre: horror, action, comedy, drama, music video...
• Gemma only rewrites when the idea, photos, length or its seed change.
• Change HOW it writes (tone, style, rules): edit 'Gemma instructions' in plain English.
• Accent is Kiwi unless your idea says otherwise.
• Write it all yourself: AUTO-PROMPTER = false, then fill in II THE SORTING GATE.
